notes: §1985:X.5.3.2 prints CANCEL { identifier-1 | literal-1 } …, one or more operands and no program-prototype-name (a 2002 addition). The grammar's cancelStatement takes cancelTarget+ (zero operands is COBOL0001), and CallBinder.BindCancel binds each target as literal-1 (through ProgramName, which refuses a non-alphanumeric literal, §1985:X.5.3.3 SR1 'Literal-1 must be a nonnumeric literal') or identifier-1; the prototype arm is reached only when ProgramPrototypeNamesExist (the program-prototype-name-2002 construct), so at 85 a bare word that names no data item is the undefined-reference error COBOL1639. Probes at --std 85: (b) CANCEL with no operand COBOL0001, a prototype-style word COBOL1639, SPACE / ALL "SUBP" / 123 COBOL1627; (c) N"SUBP" and X"53554250" COBOL0900; (d) an alphanumeric group, a reference-modified WS-LONG(1:4), a subscripted WS-T(WS-I) and FUNCTION UPPER-CASE each cancelled SUBP (COUNT 1 twice); a numeric-edited item and FUNCTION LENGTH COBOL1696; three operands with an uncalled program first ran clean. The witness cancels by literal and by identifier plus literal in one statement.

next.reason: 1985: "CANCEL { identifier-1 | literal-1 } …"; 2023: "CANCEL { identifier-1 | literal-1 | program-prototype-name-1 } …". The 2023 format adds program-prototype-name-1 as a third operand choice, so it accepts CANCEL statements that the 1985 format refuses.
